reason: All 3 immutable criteria are MET behaviourally, harness compliance is 5/5 clean, and there is no unintended production change -- but I found TWO surviving mutants that Main's matrix did not cover, and they hit the exact property this P1 step delivers. C1 MET: test_the_job_the_scheduler_received_actually_reaches_compute_freshness pulls the callable off the stub scheduler and EXECUTES it (test file :120-147); I proved it is behavioural by killing the main.py call-deletion mutant with the AST guard (:161-191) and confirming the old substring scan still returns True on that same mutant -- Main's self-reported M4 survival at experiment_results section 3.1 is TRUE, not narrative. C2 MET: test_breaching_source_pages_through_the_real_notification_path (:199-223) uses NO notify= injection, so run_freshness_check resolves raise_cron_alert_sync itself; my own ERRTYPE mutant (per-table error_type -> constant) was KILLED by it. The P1-severity claim is verified at backend/services/observability/alerting.py:54 (_CRITICAL_SEVERITIES) and :217-222 (empty webhook -> _bot_token_fallback for critical only, lower severities logged and dropped), so the severity assertion is load-bearing as claimed. C3 MET: test_all_healthy_emits_no_alert (:293-306) carries a precondition assertion that overall_band != red so a broken fixture cannot manufacture a false zero, and the autouse reset_transition_state fixture (:90-97) stops the transition gate masking the band. DETERMINISTIC, all re-run by me: immutable command BARE_EXIT=0 / 13 passed (run unpiped -- the piped form masks the exit code in zsh, which uses pipestatus); ruff F821,F401,F811 exit 0 over a DERIVED 4-file scope from git status --porcelain (git diff --name-only HEAD would have silently missed BOTH new untracked files); import smoke OK with signature (bq, cycle_interval_sec, *, emit_alarm: bool = True); scoped sweep 121 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed; verify_phase_25_A7.py 11/11. LIVE CHECK REPRODUCED BY ME, not read from Main: curl http://localhost:8000/api/jobs/all shows freshness_evaluator with next_run 2026-08-05T23:38:38.142553+02:00, matching Main's report exactly. Main's disclosure that the live check does NOT prove Slack delivery is complete and honest, and the section-5 pre-existing-failure claim is verified independently -- I reproduced test_paper_trader_execute_buy_average_up_recomputes_avg_entry and read its cause directly (assert None is not None at :627, caused by 'kill_switch: REFUSING BUY AAPL ($600.00) -- the kill switch is PAUSED (pause_reason=manual)'), which is ambient operator state unreachable from this diff. THE BLOCKER FOR PASS: test_registers_exactly_one_job_on_a_stub_scheduler (:105-117) asserts job['id'], job['replace_existing'] and job['func'] but never job['trigger'] or job['hours'], so NOTHING in the suite pins the job's RECURRENCE. My mutants trigger='interval'->'date' (fires once at startup, then the job is gone) and DEFAULT_INTERVAL_HOURS 6->99999 (~11 years) each pass all 13 tests. Both are real behavioural differentials, not equivalent mutants, and either one restores the browser-blind defect 82.10 exists to kill while shipping green. I confirmed _StubScheduler already records both keys (measured: trigger='interval', hours=6 on the captured dict), so the fix is a one-line, zero-cost addition to an existing test. This is a guard-coverage gap, not a criterion miss and not a false claim -- I grepped the handoff and Main makes NO completeness/exhaustiveness claim about the matrix, which is correct discipline per qa.md 4c. Hence CONDITIONAL, not FAIL. Harness compliance 5/5: research_brief_82.10.md 17:31:23 < contract_82.10.md 17:33:33 / contract.md 17:33:40 < code 17:37:39-41 < experiment_results 17:40:20; gate_passed true with 7 sources read in full (>=5), recency scan performed, 30 URLs; contract.md is byte-identical to contract_82.10.md and carries all 3 criteria plus the verification command VERBATIM; log-last is CORRECT -- no 'phase=82.10 result=' header exists in harness_log.md (the 3 literal '82.10' hits are all 'Next:' prose lines, checked with grep -F per the escaped-dot lesson) and masterplan 82.10 is still status=pending; cycle 1 with 0 prior CONDITIONALs, so the 3rd-CONDITIONAL auto-FAIL rule does not fire. violation_details.action: Independent mutation run (in-memory sys.modules injection, CONTROL 13/13 and POST-RESTORE 13/13 both clean): mutant A rewrote register_freshness_cron's trigger="interval" to trigger="date"; mutant B rewrote DEFAULT_INTERVAL_HOURS = 6 to 99999. Each was executed against the full immutable verification command.
violation_details.state: BOTH SURVIVED -- rc=0, '13 passed' for each. backend/tests/test_phase_82_10_freshness_paging.py:105-117 (test_registers_exactly_one_job_on_a_stub_scheduler) asserts job['id'], job['replace_existing'] is True, and job['func'] is run_freshness_check, but never asserts job['trigger'] or job['hours']. Measured directly against _StubScheduler: the captured kwargs are ['hours','id','name','replace_existing','trigger'] with trigger='interval', hours=6 -- both values are ALREADY on the recorded dict, so no new fixture or plumbing is needed. A 'date' trigger fires once at process start and never recurs; a 99999-hour interval is ~11 years. Either mutant leaves an evaluator that is scheduled in name only, functionally re-creating the browser-blind blind spot the step exists to close, and ships with a fully green suite. Both are genuine behavioural differentials versus the 6-hourly baseline, not equivalent mutants. Mitigating and weighed: the live capture I re-curled myself (freshness_evaluator next_run 2026-08-05T23:38:38.142553+02:00, ~6h after the 17:38 restart) does observe the real shipped cadence on the running service, and Main makes no completeness claim about the mutation matrix -- so this is a coverage gap, not an overclaim.
violation_details.constraint: SEVERITY: WARN (forces CONDITIONAL, not FAIL). qa.md section 4c -- for EACH immutable criterion, name the CONCRETE MUTATION that would make its guard fail; a guard that cannot fail when its subject is broken does not count. Criterion 1 ('a scheduled evaluator invokes compute_freshness ... asserted by a test against a stub scheduler') is literally and behaviourally MET, so per the 4c verdict wiring this is a WARN-level finding alongside a genuine behavioural guard, not a blocking sole-coverage vacuity. NAMED FIX (one line, zero cost, no new fixture): in test_registers_exactly_one_job_on_a_stub_scheduler add `assert job['trigger'] == 'interval'` and `assert job['hours'] == DEFAULT_INTERVAL_HOURS`. Re-run the two mutants above to confirm both then die.

notes: WRITE-FIRST SIDECAR COULD NOT BE CREATED -- DISCLOSED, NOT CIRCUMVENTED. The spawn prompt directed me to write handoff/current/qa_returns/82.10_verdict_cycle1.md incrementally. Both that path AND a scratchpad fallback were BLOCKED by the enforced PreToolUse hook .claude/hooks/qa-write-guard.sh ("qa-write-guard: BLOCKED -- the qa evaluator is read-only on file contents (Write/Edit allowed only under .claude/agent-memory/qa/)"). I treated the hook as authoritative over the spawn instruction and did not attempt any workaround (no Bash redirects, no tee, no sed). Consequence: this structured return is the ONLY copy of the verdict -- if the rail drops it, nothing is recoverable, which is exactly the risk the directive was written to remove. Main should either widen the guard to allow handoff/current/qa_returns/ or drop the sidecar clause from the Q/A spawn prompt, since the two currently contradict each other. TOOL-SURFACE NOTE: this Workflow launch did not expose SendMessage or the Playwright browser tools, so I could not message Main mid-run about the block. No UI claims are made by this step, so the 1c live-UI capture gate does not apply; the 1d backend runtime smoke gate DOES apply and I satisfied it myself (imports + live curl taken BY the evaluator, not read from Main's artifact). TWO NOTE-LEVEL OBSERVATIONS, non-blocking, offered for the follow-up rather than as verdict drivers: (1) test_evaluator_has_no_web_dependency (:150-158) bans only fastapi/starlette/TestClient/httpx/requests -- urllib, urlopen and aiohttp are NOT in the list, so a mutant routing through urllib.request would slip that particular scan; this is harmless in practice because the criterion-1 spy test would still catch it (an out-of-process HTTP call cannot trip an in-process patch of backend.services.cycle_health.compute_freshness), which is why it is NOTE and not WARN. (2) test_main_wires_the_cron_at_startup requires an ast.Call node but not that the call is REACHABLE, so a call buried in a dead branch would pass; the live /api/jobs/all capture covers this in practice. POSITIVE FINDINGS WORTH RECORDING, since qa.md asks for success signal and not only defects: the anti-vacuity work here is genuinely above this project's recent baseline. Main proactively disclosed in experiment_results section 3.1 that mutant M4 SURVIVED the first version of its own guard and rewrote a substring scan into an AST check -- I verified BOTH halves independently rather than accepting the story ("register_freshness_cron" in mutated_src still evaluates True with the call deleted, and the AST guard raises the intended AssertionError), so the self-report is accurate and the fix is real. The criterion-2 test deliberately omits notify= injection so the evaluator resolves raise_cron_alert_sync through its own production import, which is the strong form of that guard rather than the convenient one. The autouse reset_transition_state fixture and the two precondition assertions ("fixture did not breach", "all-green fixture computed overall_band=...") specifically defend against passing-for-the-wrong-reason, and Main's own F1 fixture mutant exercises them. Scope honesty in section 7 is accurate as written: I confirmed the HTTP call sites are untouched, emit_alarm is keyword-only with default True so the three positional callers are behaviourally unchanged, and the deliberate decision to skip misfire_grace_time/coalesce is justified by a checkable fact (main.py constructs a bare AsyncIOScheduler with the default in-memory jobstore, so nothing persists across restart to replay). Finally, the pre-existing-failure disclosure did not rely on my trusting the worktree run -- I reproduced the failure and read the kill-switch refusal in the captured log, so the claim stands on my own measurement. RECOMMENDED PATH TO PASS: add the two one-line assertions named in violation_details to the existing stub-scheduler test, re-run my two surviving mutants to confirm they die, update experiment_results with that matrix delta, then spawn a FRESH Q/A on the CHANGED evidence -- that is the documented cycle-2 flow, not verdict-shopping, because the files will have changed between spawns.
